notes:
Cards and offloads
- Sony cards with M4ROOT at the root of the volume (the FX6 / a1 in MP4 mode) are recognised: the clips come from M4ROOT/CLIP with their XML sidecars and the camera is named from the card's own metadata.
- A DJI Mic (and any audio-only recorder card) is a recorder, not an unrecognised camera. Empty card-reader slots are no longer offered as cards.
- A card of nothing but JPEGs (a timelapse) no longer hangs the offload window, and identifies its camera from the photos rather than a stale thumbnail.
- An unrecognised card is copied whole only after you say so: Start Transfer asks first, with the file count, size and destination.
- The whole-card copy honours your selection, shows real progress and can be cancelled. The Start Transfer press and any refusal are in the log.
- Ejecting a card on Windows works again (the documented Win32 eject, with a real wait for the card to leave); Mac eject is unchanged.
- The clips reach DaVinci Resolve first, at full speed, and the day timelines are placed before analysis starts. A 219-clip card that took a morning is minutes again.
- A clip's gyro telemetry is read once, not once per lane.
- A resumed offload hands its timelapse to Resolve as an image sequence, and a timelapse is one tile in the Media band (right-click to show the frames).
- Selecting or deselecting files in a large card no longer freezes the window.

Timelines and Resolve
- Every time-of-day timeline is filed in Timelines / Time of Day (a sibling of Rough Cuts). Resync moves the ones already elsewhere.
- Clips with no clock get their own "clips with no time" timeline instead of being guessed onto a day, and the 613 such clips in one project are now named, not just counted.
- Resync works on the first click: the open-and-resync route applies the day it built.
- Catalog: "Add N at playhead" places the selection on the open timeline at the playhead, honouring moment marks.
- Transcribing through DaVinci Resolve: an instant refusal is Resolve not being ready, so the clip waits and is retried instead of being marked failed. Cut Valet also backs off when Resolve is the one using the machine's memory, and says so.

Analysis
- Rich describe: a camera thumbnail stream (DJI Osmo Pocket) made every frame grab come back empty; frames are grabbed from the real video stream now.
- The describe row lists the cloud provider's actual vision models (Luna, Sol, Terra, Claude, Gemini) instead of a provider, and the frames go to the model you picked. The Detail dial redraws the numbers under it.
- A cloud describe no longer holds the GPU, so transcription, embeddings and faces run alongside it. The log names the cloud brain that described a clip.
- A timelapse is analysed once as a run, not once per frame.
- A pinned Ollama context window is honoured everywhere, and a refusal points at Settings > AI > Context window.
- "Run on N clips" no longer freezes the window on a large selection; deselected jobs read as off; Adopt then Close shows the adopted project straight away.

App
- Opening a project whose folder sits on a sleeping network share no longer freezes the app.
- "Update when it's done" waits until the work has actually finished, and the update card's presses are logged.
- Quit no longer waits ten minutes for a description in flight.
added: Time of day sync, for lining up a whole day of cameras.
Tech stack, which scans this computer and tunes itself.
Ingest is a page, so several cards can land at once.
The assistant says what it knows, and every line has a switch.
